names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 6 Δεκεμβρίου, «Όσιος Νείλος «ὁ ἐν τῇ νήσῳ Στολοβνόε ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ Σεληγέρα» ο Νέος και θαυματουργός», with the rank words left off. The place and the by-names are left off the stored form.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 7. децембар ст. ст., „Преподобни Нил Столбенски.“ — with «Преподобни» left off, that being the `venerable` grade `types` keeps. «Столбенски» is the island of Stolobnoe and not a rank, it is what tells him from the other Nilus folders, and §6 asks for the fullest form the calendar gives; the Greek form stored here is the bare «Νείλος» with the island taken off, so the two forms differ in exactly that and the fuller one is this book’s. `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the folded string at 0 other holders.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru’s line for 7 декабря ст. ст., «Преподобный Нил Столобенский», with the rank word left off. The folder's Serbian form spells the island «Столбенски» and this one «Столобенский». The line on the day page itself gives the name in the genitive.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 декабря ст. ст. — «Прп. Нила Столобенского (1554).»

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, and the same man and the same menologion day the Serbian row already keeps; the Greek row keeps him one day earlier, on 6 December, which is that calendar's own placement and is left as it stands. The year the line closes with, 1554, is the year this folder already holds for his death, read off the Ohrid Prologue. `types` and `dates` untouched.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 6ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Νείλος «ὁ ἐν τῇ νήσῳ Στολοβνόε ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ Σεληγέρα» ο Νέος και θαυματουργός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 6 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and its whole content is «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Ρώσου Οσίου» — we have no details of the Russian venerable's life. No year, so no `dates` object; the island and the lake are named only in the day's line and no coordinate is proposed from them. The corpus keeps `germanos-of-stolobnoe` from the Greek 22 February, whose own saint.gr page describes his hermitage as the desert of Saint Nilus at Stolobnoe; that is the other page's sentence and not this one's, so no `related` row is made and nothing in the Germanos folder is touched. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.12.2025 (7. децембар ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Нил Столбенски.“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. A DIFFERENT DAY FROM THE GREEK ONE: saint.gr keeps him on 6 December and this book on the Julian 7 December. The serbian row was `undocumented`, so the row lands on this book’s day and the greek row is untouched. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Преподобни» is the `venerable` held, `wonderworker` was there, and «земљорадник» — a tiller of the soil — is a trade and no rank; `hermit` was NOT added, because the book says he withdrew into the wilderness without using any of the rank words BRIEF-SERBIAN §5 maps to it. `dates` ADDED, and it is the first date of any kind this folder has carried: «Упокојио се и преселио у Царство Христово 1554. године» — he reposed and passed over into the kingdom of Christ in 1554. saint.gr gives no year. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS IS THE WHOLE OF HIS STORY, where the Greek line gave only the island, the lake and the two by-names: that he was a tiller of the soil, a native of Novgorod; that having withdrawn into the wilderness he fed on herbs and husks; that he moved to the island of Stolobnoe at a voice from above; that robbers once came into his cell to plunder it and were struck blind on the instant; that he dug himself a grave beside the cell and wept over it every day; and that his wonderworking relics rest in the place where he had fasted. NO `locations`: Novgorod, the wilderness and the island of Stolobnoe are three places and the folder has never held a coordinate. NO `related` row: the entry names nobody. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: Охридски пролог за 7. децембар ст. ст.: „Упокојио се и преселио у Царство Христово 1554. године.“ — he reposed and passed over into the kingdom of Christ in 1554. The first date of any kind this folder has carried: saint.gr names the island, the lake and the two by-names and gives no year at all, and this folder's `dates` was null before this reading.

hymns.text: Яко светильник всесветел,/ явился еси во острове Селигера езера,/ преподобне отче Ниле,/ ты бо, крест Христов от юности своея на рамо взем,/ усердно Тому последовал еси,/ чистотою Богови приближився,/ отонудуже и чудес дарованием обогатился еси./ Тем и мы, притекающе к раце мощей твоих, умильно глаголем:/ отче преподобне,/ моли Христа Бога// спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 декабря ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобного Нила Столобенского»

english.text: You appeared as a lamp giving light on every side upon the island of Lake Seliger, venerable father Nilus; for taking the cross of Christ on your shoulder from your youth you followed him with zeal, and drawing near to God by purity you were enriched from there with the gift of wonders. Therefore we too, running to the shrine of your relics, say with compunction: Venerable father, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Отечества, преподобне, удалився,/ в пустыню вселился еси,/ и, на остров Селигера езера возшед,/ жестоко житие показал еси,/ и, многих добродетельми удивив,/ дарования чудес от Христа приял еси./ Поминай нас, чтущих память твою, да зовем ти:// радуйся, Ниле, отче наш.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 декабря ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобного Нила Столобенского»

english.text: Going away from your own country, venerable one, you settled in the wilderness; and having come up onto the island of Lake Seliger you showed a hard way of life, and astonishing many by your virtues you received from Christ the gift of wonders. Remember us who honour your memory, that we may cry to you: Rejoice, Nilus our father.
